the regulation of arginine-supply mechanisms in activated microglia.
the regulation of the arginine metabolism in activated microglia and its role in NO synthesis.
the regulation of NO production by activated microglial cell and the possible involvement of NO in the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative disorders.

argininosuccinase and CAT-2 play an important role for NO production by activated microglial cell.
the induction of iNOS, CAT-2, and AS in activated microglia is a key factor in NO production.

the expression of AS, CAT-2, and iNOS is co-induced in activated microglia, and that the induction of AS and CAT-2 is essential for high-output production and prolonged release of NO.

microglia have a mechanism for recycling arginine and citrullines to maintain NO production in the presence of a low concentration of extracellular arginine.
the microglia are capable of producing a lot of nitric oxide, and this production is dependent on the presence of arginine.
